answer.rationale: Finance mandate of 18% spend cut is incompatible with the incumbent's refusal to reopen price, so renewal cannot deliver the required unit-cost reduction. memory_c2 documents that switching primary supply to the low-cost vendor produced a sharp unit-cost cut with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, which directly supports the only lever available this cycle for an 18% reduction. I want to verify memory_c6 first because it carries the competing signal — long incumbency unlocked volume pricing and narrower service — that could underweight the savings from a switch or reveal hidden integration overhead. With one decision available, the choice must be the move that most reliably closes the 18% gap; verification of c6 just confirms whether volume-tier savings on a multi-year are actually forgone vs. preserved, which sharpens the cost model but does not change the action.
